blocks.body: Hydro jetting clears a sewer line with a high-pressure water stream, fed through the same cleanout access point used for rodding. A specialized nozzle sprays water in every direction as it moves through the pipe, scouring grease, scale, and roots off the entire pipe wall instead of just cutting a path through the middle. It's the fix for buildup that keeps coming back after rodding, or for roots that have worked into the pipe joints. Rodding opens the line back up. Hydro jetting cleans it.

img.alt: Diagram showing how hydro jetting clears a residential sewer line, with a cross-section view of the underground pipe, jet nozzle, high-pressure water spray, and debris being flushed toward the street connection

blocks.h2: When Your Plumbing Needs Hydro Jetting
blocks.intro: Hydro jetting clears buildup off the entire pipe wall, not just the one clog blocking it right now. Here's how to know it's time to call:

tiles.h3: Drains Gurgle When the Washer Empties
tiles.body: If your drains gurgle or the basement floor drain backs up when the washing machine empties, water can't get past something in the main line. On tree-lined streets, that something is often roots.

tiles.h3: Roots Have Worked Into the Pipe Joints
tiles.body: Roots find any gap in a pipe joint and grow into the line chasing moisture. A rod clears what's blocking flow right now, but it doesn't stop what's growing at the next joint down the line.

tiles.h3: Buildup Has Hardened on the Pipe Wall
tiles.body: Grease, scale, and sludge coat the inside of the pipe over time. A rod cuts a path through the middle, but it doesn't remove what's stuck to the walls.

tiles.h3: The Clog Keeps Coming Back After Rodding
tiles.body: Rodding breaks through the immediate blockage, but it leaves buildup on the pipe walls that the next clog catches on. Hydro jetting clears what rodding leaves behind.

blocks.h2: Why Highland Park Sewer Lines Clog
blocks.intro: Highland Park has two things that are hard on sewer lines: older homes and big trees. Nearly half of the homes here were built before 1960, and about 1 in 4 before 1940. Many still have their original clay sewer pipe.

items.h3: Older Clay Pipe With Aging Joints
items.body: Clay sewer pipe comes in short sections joined end to end. As a line ages and the ground shifts, those joints open small gaps. Grease and scale catch on the edges, and roots find their way in. Hydro jetting cleans the whole pipe wall, so the next clog has less to catch on.

items.h3: Ravines, Mature Trees and Root Intrusion
items.body: Highland Park's ravines and tree-lined streets put a lot of roots close to sewer lines. Roots grow toward moisture and slip into older pipe at the joints. Hydro jetting cuts them out and flushes them away. Roots do grow back, so a [camera inspection](/highland-park/video-camera-sewer-inspections) shows where they're getting in, and you can decide if a [sewer repair](/highland-park/sewer-repair) makes sense.

items.h3: Your Sewer Line Is Your Responsibility
items.body: In Highland Park, the homeowner owns and maintains the private sewer line from the house to the city main. When roots or buildup block it, the fix is on you, not the city. The city's own flood tips recommend having your sewer line checked for roots and debris. A clean line, backed by an [overhead sewer system](/highland-park/overhead-sewer-systems) or other [basement flood protection](/highland-park/basement-flooding), gives heavy rain less of a chance to push water back into your basement.

blocks.h2: Hydro Jetting Questions From Highland Park Homeowners

items.q: Is hydro jetting safe for the old clay pipe in my home?
items.preview: Yes, when the pipe is checked first. We run a camera before any jetting to confirm what the line can handle.
items.answer: Yes, when the pipe is checked first. About 1 in 4 Highland Park homes was built before 1940, and many older lines are clay. We run a camera through the line before any jetting, so we know if a section is cracked or broken. If the pipe can't take the pressure, we'll tell you and walk you through other options, like [sewer rodding](/highland-park/sewer-rodding) or a [sewer repair](/highland-park/sewer-repair).

items.q: Who is responsible for the sewer line in Highland Park, the city or the homeowner?
items.preview: The homeowner. You own the private sewer line from your house to the city main.
items.answer: The homeowner. In Highland Park, you own and maintain the private sewer line that runs from your house to the city main. If roots or buildup block that line, the fix is yours to handle. We can inspect it, clean it and show you its condition on camera.

items.q: How often should I hydro jet my sewer line if I have big trees?
items.preview: When roots are the cause, results usually last one to three years. A camera inspection shows how fast they're coming back.
items.answer: It depends on how fast roots come back in your line. Most homeowners with root intrusion see results last one to three years before the line needs maintenance again. Homes near mature trees or ravines may need it on the shorter end of that range. A camera inspection shows how much has grown back, and [regular sewer maintenance](/highland-park/sewer-maintenance) keeps it from turning into a backup.

items.preview: It depends on the problem. Snaking is fast and effective for most clogs; hydro jetting is the stronger fix for hardened buildup or root intrusion.
items.answer: It depends on the problem. A drain snake breaks through a clog to restore flow. It's fast, effective, and the right call for most drain issues. Hydro jetting uses high-pressure water to scour the pipe wall clean from the inside. When buildup has hardened on the pipe wall, roots have worked into the joints, or the same clog keeps coming back after rodding, hydro jetting is the stronger fix. A camera inspection tells us which one your line actually needs.

items.q: How much does hydro jetting cost in Highland Park?
items.preview: Cost depends on the length of the line, the severity of the buildup, and what the camera inspection finds. We quote pricing upfront.
items.answer: Hydro jetting cost depends on the length of the line, the severity of the buildup, and what the camera inspection finds. Older clay lines with heavy root growth can take more work to clear. Every job starts with a diagnosis. We show you exactly what's in the pipe and give you pricing upfront before any work begins. No surprises once we get started.

items.preview: It clears roots that have already worked into the line, but it can't stop new roots from growing back.
items.answer: It can cut through and flush out roots that have worked their way into pipe joints, clearing the line completely. What it can't do is stop roots from growing back. That requires repairing or relining the pipe where the intrusion is happening. The camera inspection shows exactly where the roots are entering so you know what you're dealing with before you decide.

items.q: Why do plumbers not like Drano?
items.preview: It works chemically, not mechanically, and can corrode older pipes over time without clearing buildup from the walls.
items.answer: The issue isn't that it doesn't work. It's that it works chemically, not mechanically. Drano dissolves organic material, but it can also corrode older pipes over time, especially the cast iron and clay lines common in older homes. It also doesn't remove buildup from pipe walls the way hydro jetting does. It just clears a path through the clog. For a slow drain or minor backup, it might buy you time. For a recurring problem, it's masking something that needs to be properly diagnosed.
